problem_motivation.content: Conventional material processing achieves strengthening only by sacrificing ductility.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Conventional material processing approaches often achieve strengthening of materials at the cost of reduced ductility.

problem_motivation.content: Conventional processing strategies achieve high strength at the expense of ductility, and developing structures that improve both simultaneously remains highly challenging.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Unfortunately, conventional processing strategies usually attain high material strength at the expense of deteriorated ductility [1] – [3] , whilst developing structures with substantial improvement of both strength and ductility is highly challenging.

problem_motivation.content: Predicting and interpreting mechanical behaviors of HPHT-treated materials, especially regarding non-equilibrium interfaces, remains difficult due to complex parameter spaces and microstructural evolution.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Given the vast space of control parameters involved in the HPHT treatment and the often complex microstructural evolution under extreme pressures and temperatures [9] , [10] , it remains difficult to predict and interpret the mechanical behaviors of HPHT-treated structural materials, especially the abnormal kinetics and thermodynamics of non-equilibrium interfaces induced by the HPHT treatment [11] , [12] .

prior_approach.content: Traditional processing of eutectic high entropy alloys results in interfacial cracking.
prior_approach.evidence_span: commonly observed in traditional eutectic high entropy alloys

prior_limitation.content: Traditional eutectic high entropy alloys suffer from interfacial cracking.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: arresting interfacial cracking commonly observed in traditional eutectic high entropy alloys

prior_limitation.content: Room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility hinder the practical application of eutectic high entropy alloys.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, the room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility of these alloys hinder their usage in practical applications

causal_claim.content: HPHT treatment caused a doubling of both strength and tensile ductility.
causal_claim.evidence_span: simultaneously doubling its strength to 1150 MPa and its tensile ductility to 36% after the HPHT treatment

causal_claim.content: Reduction in strength of as-cast samples is attributed to microstructure changes induced by HPHT treatment.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The reduction in strength of the Ac samples can be attributed to the change in the microstructure with HPHT treatment (Supplementary Note 3 ).

mechanism_principle.content: The strength-ductility synergy is caused by HPHT-induced hierarchical microstructures promoting multiple deformation mechanisms.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Such strength-ductility synergy is attributed to the HPHT-induced formation of a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces, which promotes multiple deformation mechanisms

mechanism_principle.content: The microstructure relieves stress concentration, preventing interfacial cracking.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the HPHT-induced microstructure helps relieve stress concentration at the interfaces, thereby arresting interfacial cracking

mechanism_principle.content: The coherent interface allows dislocation transfer, alleviating stress concentration and coordinating deformation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Dislocations preferentially initiate in the softer FCC phase, and subsequently are allowed to transfer into the harder B2 phase due to the highly coherent interface, which effectively alleviates stress concentration at the interface and coordinates deformation between the two phases.

mechanism_principle.content: The hierarchically patterned structure with a coherent interface activates multiple mechanisms (SFs, microbands, twins) to accommodate plasticity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Overall, the hierarchically patterned structure with the coherent interface (Fig. 1 h–l) not only confines dislocation slip, but more importantly, it also provides a route to accommodate plasticity through the activation of multiple deformation mechanisms, including SFs, microbands and deformation twins (illustrated in Fig. 4j ), thus endowing the alloy with excellent structural stability and strain-hardening capability.

hypothesis_statement.content: HPHT treatment can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) treatment can help overcome the strength-ductility trade-off

hypothesis_statement.content: The hierarchically patterned structure with coherent interfaces, achieved through HPHT treatment, is expected to significantly improve the mechanical response, a result typically inaccessible to conventional processing.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The hierarchically patterned structure with coherent interfaces modulated through HPHT treatment is expected to have a major impact on the mechanical response of the HPHT-treated alloy, which is generally inaccessible to conventional materials processing techniques.

hypothesis_statement.content: The HPHT strategy is proposed as a general pathway applicable to pure metal copper and other alloy systems.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In view of the adjustable pressure, temperature, and chamber size of the self-designed hexahedron-anvil-press apparatus, the HPHT strategy can be generally applied to pure metal copper (Supplementary Fig. 22 ) and other alloy systems (Supplementary Fig. 23 and Supplementary Fig. 24 ), making it an appealing pathway to the design and fabrication of advanced structural materials with extraordinary mechanical properties.

evidence_result.content: HPHT treatment resulted in nearly 100% enhancement in strength (~1150 MPa) and tensile ductility (36%) compared to the Ho alloy.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The HPHT-treated alloy exhibits nearly 100% enhancement in both strength (~1150 MPa) and tensile ductility (36%) compared with the Ho alloy.

evidence_result.content: Conventional hot isostatic pressing and thermal-mechanical treatments did not produce the same synergistic strength-ductility enhancement observed with HPHT.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Such HPHT-induced synergistic enhancement in strength and ductility is not observed in our experiments with conventional hot isostatic pressing treatment (Supplementary Fig. 5 ) and thermal-mechanical treatment (Supplementary Fig. 6 ).

evidence_result.content: HPHT-treated alloy shows a work-hardening capability that is more pronounced and stable up to the tensile plastic instability region compared to other alloys.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In comparison with the Ac, Ac+HPHT and Ho alloys, the work-hardening capability of HPHT-treated alloy is much more pronounced and stable up to the tensile plastic instability region.

evidence_result.content: Fracture surface analysis reveals high density of microcracks and unbroken ligaments in the HPHT-treated alloy, unlike the elongated cracks in the Ho alloy.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Different from the elongated cracks with large width along the interfaces in the fractured Ho alloy, a high density of microcracks and a more uniform crack surface morphology can be observed in the HPHT-treated alloy (Supplementary Fig. 10 ).

evidence_result.content: EBSD analysis confirms the hierarchically patterned microstructure and dual-phase structure are preserved even after extended uniform elongation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, the featured hierarchically patterned microstructure is well preserved during loading, which can even be observed faintly on the fracture surface after the extended uniform elongation, indicating the high structural stability of the HPHT-treated alloy.

evidence_result.content: GND density evolution in the HPHT-treated alloy shows the B2 phase eventually matching the FCC phase density at 35% strain, indicating homogeneous deformation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Upon further loading, the GND density of the B2 phase increases much faster than that of the FCC phase, eventually resulting in an identical value of GND density in both phases at 35% strain, consistent with a homogeneous plastic deformation distribution (Fig. 3c ).

evidence_result.content: GND densities in the HPHT-treated alloy are significantly higher than in the Ho alloy, indicating an improved capability for dislocation storage.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Moreover, the GND densities in the HPHT alloy are much higher than those in the Ho alloy, indicating improved capability of dislocation storage in the HPHT-treated alloy.

constraint.content: The electro-polishing process for specimen preparation was constrained to specific chemical composition, voltage, and temperature conditions.
constraint.evidence_span: prepared by electro-polishing in a solution of HNO 3 (20%) and C 2 H 5 OH (80%) with a voltage of 20 V at 233 K
